ANALYSIS: "Interstitial cystitis" (IC) is a historical term that has evolved into the broader diagnostic construct "Interstitial Cystitis/Bladder Pain Syndrome" (IC/BPS), as endorsed by major urologic societies (e.g., AUA, EAU). IC/BPS is defined by chronic pelvic pain, pressure, or discomfort perceived to be related to the bladder, accompanied by urinary symptoms (e.g., urgency, frequency), in the absence of infection or other identifiable cause. The "non-ulcerative type" refers to the more common presentation (≈90% of cases) without Hunner’s lesions (ulcers) on cystoscopy — distinguishing it from the less common "ulcerative" (Hunner’s lesion) subtype. Thus, the predicted diagnosis uses current, precise terminology and correctly specifies the most prevalent clinical variant. It is not contradictory but rather an updated, more nuanced formulation of the same condition.

VERDICT: CORRECT
